grammar.label: the colon and the semicolon
grammar.form: clause : list or explanation; clause ; closely related clause

explanation.en: A colon promises that what follows explains or lists what came before: it must have a complete clause on its left. A semicolon joins two clauses that could each stand alone; it is stronger than a comma and weaker than a full stop. A comma cannot do either job.
explanation.uz: Ikki nuqta chapidagi gapni izohlaydi yoki ro'yxat keltiradi va chap tomonda to'liq gap bo'lishi shart. Nuqtali vergul mustaqil ikki gapni bog'laydi. Oddiy vergul bu vazifalarni bajara olmaydi.

grammar.positive_example: The cause was simple: nobody had checked the date.
grammar.negative_example: The cause was simple, nobody had checked the date.

l1_notes.uz: Rus tilida ikki nuqta va nuqtali vergul boshqacha qo'llanadi; ingliz qoidasi chap tomonda to'liq gap talab qiladi.

grammar.label: parenthesis — commas, brackets and dashes
grammar.form: clause, aside, clause / clause (aside) clause / clause — aside — clause

explanation.en: The three mark the same structure at different volumes: commas are quietest, brackets push the aside furthest down, dashes are loudest and most informal. Whichever you open with, you must close with — a dash cannot be closed by a comma.
explanation.uz: Uchalasi ham bir xil tuzilmani turli kuchda ajratadi: vergul — eng yumshoq, qavs — eng chetga suradi, tire — eng kuchli va norasmiy. Qaysi belgi bilan ochilsa, o'sha bilan yopiladi.

grammar.positive_example: The report — all ninety pages of it — arrived on Friday.
grammar.negative_example: The report — all ninety pages of it, arrived on Friday.

l1_notes.uz: Ochilgan belgi albatta yopilishi kerak — bu eng keng tarqalgan tinish belgisi xatosi.

body.speaker: Sarah
body.text: You have used a colon here and a semicolon two lines down. Tell me why.

body.speaker: Aziz
body.text: The colon promises a list. Three artefacts came out of the excavation: a cup, a knife and a coin.

body.speaker: Aziz
body.text: Two sentences that belong together. 'The parchment is safe; the papyrus is not.'

body.speaker: Aziz
body.text: I have three dashes on one page.

body.speaker: Sarah
body.text: Two too many. A dash is a raised voice. Raise it once.

body.speaker: Aziz
body.text: So the aside goes in brackets instead?

body.speaker: Sarah
body.text: Brackets if the reader may skip it. Commas if the reader may not.

body.speaker: Aziz
body.text: 'The codex, which nobody has opened since 1974, is the whole reason for the visit.'

body.speaker: Sarah
body.text: Commas, and the reader keeps it. Good.

body.speaker: Aziz
body.text: The index at the back is three pages.

body.speaker: Sarah
body.text: Then somebody will use it, which is more than most of us can say for our epilogues.
